analysis:
All changes are in the ProviderBenchmark target and look like API-compatibility adjustments to an upstream dependency. I found no security-relevant behavior change.

- MTPProductionSession.swift:115 only module-qualifies the call as MLXLLM.Gemma4AssistantDraftModel.load(from:). The assistant directory is still local-only, with no download. Loading, drafter binding, the benchmark-only prefix-cache override (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 at line 226) and the stop-token policy are unchanged. The benchmark engine still disables the SSD prefix cache, so the T-041 at-rest surface is not touched.
- ModelBenchmark.swift:256 adds a .rejectedToolCall case to the Generation switch and ignores it, like .toolCall. This benchmark-only code never reaches the coordinator, so no plaintext, attestation or authorization path is affected.
- ThroughputSweep.swift:127, 219, 224, 227 and 237 make measurePrefill throwing and use try on ctx.model.newCache. Errors now propagate instead of being swallowed. The patch excerpt is truncated after line 237, so the rest of the sweep was not seen. The change is fail-closed for the benchmark and has no exposure impact.

The diff implies that upstream mlx-swift-lm has changed: newCache now throws, Generation gained .rejectedToolCall, and the Gemma4 assistant type may be namespaced differently. That dependency change, and any production-path callers (for example in ProviderCore, such as the serving handling of .rejectedToolCall and the throwing newCache), are not in this batch. The next pass should check that serving code handles those new semantics fail-closed, particularly that rejected tool calls are not emitted as plaintext or silently dropped. No finding is supported from the supplied evidence. needs_deeper_review is set because that dependency interaction is unverified.
